title: Verdant Learning - Outreach & Objection Playbook (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick research + outbound copy + objection handling for Verdant Learning (mid-market LMS for higher-ed & upskilling). Goal = get intro call with Head of Product / Director Partnerships, target pilot for Q2.

Account snapshot (fast):
- Name: Verdant Learning (founded 2016)
- Product: modular LMS for universities + corporate upskilling; emphasis on competency frameworks, outcomes tracking, LTI integrations, SCORM support.
- Customers: 120 orgs (mix of regional universities + 20 enterprise customers).
- Likely pain: scaling content personalization, grading automation, embedding AI tutors while keeping PII on-prem for some clients.
- Recent signals: Series B announced (2025-09) -> hiring product leads, PR about "adaptive pathways" feature. Good time to pitch pilot.

Technical fit notes (quick tech checklist):
- Integration: supports LTI 1.3 & LTI Advantage (we can integrate via placements and deep-link).
- SSO: SAML + OIDC supported; customer might want SSO + token scoping for instructor-level vs student-level.
- Data residency: some customers ask for private deployments -> Redwood Private might be strong pitch.
- Model/capability ask: grading rubrics, short-answer evaluation, personalized reading suggestions, on-device inference for sensitive clients.

Quant metrics to surface in outbound/call:
- "Reduce instructor grading time by X%" — use conservative claims: 20–35% for short-answer sets (pilot).
- "Avg latency" promise: hosted API median token latency numbers (we'll provide bench for >= 95th pct SLA for demo).
- Cost benefit framing: show cost per grading-job vs instructor hours (example calc in demo deck).

Outbound email drafts (A/B) - short, teacher-friendly tone: 
A) Subject: Quick idea to help Verdant scale personalized feedback
Hi [Name],
I saw Verdant's piece on adaptive pathways — congrats on the Series B. We help LMS teams add scalable, reliable AI tutors and short-answer grading without changing their UX or risking student data.
Would you be open to a 20‑minute call next week to see a small pilot idea tailored to Verdant?
— Aisha (Redwood Inference)

B) Subject: Pilot: automated grading + tutor — low lift for Verdant
Hey [Name],
Two quick bullets: 1) a 6–8 week pilot that auto-evaluates short answers and surfaces high-confidence feedback to students; 2) no student data leaves your VPC (we can run Private).
Would love 15 minutes to outline scope.

Cold-call / voicemail script (30s):
"Hi [Name], Aisha at Redwood Inference — we help LMS teams like Verdant cut instructor grading time and roll out AI tutors safely. I emailed a short pilot idea — would you be open to 15 minutes on Thursday to look at a concrete scope? Thanks."

Discovery questions to ask on first call (prioritized):
- Who owns AI/ML roadmap? Product or partnerships?
- Biggest instructor pain today (grading, office-hours load, content discoverability)?
- Any privacy/regulatory constraints (FERPA, GDPR expectations, residency)?
- Current integration surface: LTI placements? API endpoints for content/gradebook?
- Pilot constraints: timeline, success metrics, decision makers?

Objections & suggested responses (short, conversational):
1) "We don't want student data leaving our systems."
  - Resp: "Totally understood. We can run Redwood Private in your VPC or on-prem for pilot, and give you audit logs + KMS integration. Many universities prefer that for grading workloads."

2) "AI grading is unreliable / unfair."
  - Resp: "We start with high‑confidence automation for clear rubrics and keep manual review hooks for edge cases. We'll define pass/fail thresholds and carry out calibration with a gold set provided by your instructors — typical accuracy uplift is visible within 2–3 sprints."

3) "Integrations are a nightmare for our product team."
  - Resp: "We have a small integration SDK and an LTI deep-link sandbox. For pilots we can do read-only gradebook syncs and push back grade suggestions rather than changing core flows."

Commercial approach ideas (pilot-first):
- 6–8 week pilot: up to 5000 student interactions, fixed professional services (PS) fee + reduced trial usage rate.
- Post-pilot options: per-seat or per-eval pricing; enterprise seat+throughput commit for Dedicated capacity if they want predictable latency.
- Offer evaluation dashboard access and one month of quality monitoring as part of pilot.

Success metrics to co-agree in pilot contract:
- Instructor time saved (hours/week aggregated)
- Precision@K for grading/rubric items (benchmarks on sample set)
- Student satisfaction (NPS or short pulse)
- Integration completion (LTI placement + gradebook sync)

Deck / demo plan (30m pilot pitch):
- 5m: quick intro + signal (why Verdant now)
- 8m: demo of grading flow & AI tutor in Verdant-like UI (show false positive guardrails)
- 7m: tech/integration approach (private vs hosted, SSO, data flow)
- 5m: pilot scope, pricing, timeline
- 5m: Q&A + next steps

Playbook notes / redlines before sending email:
- Avoid big numbers claims; use ranges and pilot-first framing.
- Tag legal early for data residency (if they ask for on-prem, we need scoping).
- Ask Diego to prep sample dataset conversion notes for their gradebook CSVs (example mapping).

Open questions / to-do (short):
- Get latest Verdant org chart (who is Head of Product + Director Partnerships?) — Maya to pull LinkedIn list.
- Verify their SCORM/LTI exact versions (reach out to Dev Evangelist thread).
- Prep a 10-minute recorded demo of grading flow using synthetic campus data (Diego).
- Draft PS estimate template for 6–8 week pilot (include engineering + integration + project mgmt).

Next immediate actions (priority order):
1) Send A/B email to Head of Product + cc Director Partnerships (use A then B as follow-up 4 days later).
2) Diego builds demo clip and maps one sample assignment.
3) Maya assembles LinkedIn contact list and searches for mutual intro.
4) Book 30m internal sync to agree on PS estimate and pilot SOW draft (this week).

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep message coachable: instructors care about speed and fairness; product cares about retention + outcomes.
- Use "pilot" language not "proof of concept" — lower friction.
- If legal delays, offer sandboxed evaluation with anonymized data first.

Random thinking / brainstorm snippets:
- Could bundle "AI tutor" + "quick rubric builder" as a single light-weight feature for 1st pilot.
- Explore channel with LTI marketplace — maybe Verdant lists partner features there.

-- end of scratch pad --
